title: Types of businesses
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No single bank point covers the whole brief: the closest, bus-sole-traders-partnerships, covers only sole traders and partnerships at Year 11 depth and omits companies and business size, while bus-size-business covers only size, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Types of businesses
card: A business owned and run by one person. The owner keeps all the profit and is personally responsible for its debts.
A business owned by two or more people who share the work, the profit and the risk.
A business that is a separate legal entity from its owners, who are called shareholders. It can own property and be sued in its own name.
Businesses are also small, medium or large, judged by things such as how many staff they employ and how much they sell. A business can be, for example, a small company or a large company.
draft.remember: Ownership type (sole trader, partnership, company) is one question and size is another.

a.q: Priya owns and runs a bike repair shop by herself. She keeps all the profit. What type of business is it?
a.why: One owner who runs the business and keeps all the profit is a sole trader. It is not a partnership, which needs two or more owners.
a.clue: Count how many owners there are.

b.q: A company called Bright Tiles Pty Ltd is sued after a faulty job. Which feature of companies explains why the case is against the business itself?
opts: It is a separate legal entity from its owners
It is owned by two or more partners
Its owner keeps all the profit
b.why: A company is a separate legal entity, so it can be sued in its own name. Sharing ownership between partners describes a partnership, not why a company is sued.
b.clue: Think about who the law treats as the business.

b.best: It is a separate legal entity from its owners
